newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SWIMMING-HUNGARIAN POLICE SAY PRE-OLYMPIC SWIM TIMES FIXED.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-HUNGARIAN POLICE SAY PRE-OLYMPIC SWIM TIMES FIXED.

text.p: A police investigation found strong evidence that Olympic qualifying times for Hungarian swimmers were falsified and a report has been forwarded to the prosecutor, a police official said on Friday.

The investigation concluded there was "well-founded suspicion" that times had been falsified by officials of the Hungarian Swimming Federation, Gyula Mizo, an official of the central police directorate, told Reuters.
The Hungarian news agency MTI reported that the swimming federation's secretary general, Jozsef Fuzsa, and former federation inspector Peter Hauer, had been charged with falsifying documents.
MTI said the police investigation revealed that, before the 1996 Atlanta Games, false information was submitted on times achieved by Hungarian swimmers in national swimming championships.
For six of the swimmers the times were better than they had ever achieved, allowing them to qualify for the Olympics, MTI said.
